newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent extends loss, reversing OPEC-led gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent extends loss, reversing OPEC-led gains.

text.p: IPE oil futures on Thursday gave up some of yesterday's OPEC-inspired gains on scepticism over pledges of output restraint, and waited for New York markets to open to drive numbers lower.
By 1200 GMT Aug Brent was 19 cents lower at $18.03 a barrel, after a hefty 34-cent gain on Wednesday following declarations by OPEC members they would cut back on their over-production.

Gas oil was up $1.50 at $161.75 a tonne , catching up on Brent's late gains yesterday. On ACCESS WTI traded 19 cents down, eating into the 49-cent gain it made in the flurry of buying sparked by the news from the OPEC meeting in Vienna.

Brokers said Brent's key support levels were $18.08 and the psychological $18.00 mark. Once both were breached, numbers would tumble, they said. WTI would face similar pressure if it buckled beneath $19.30, they added.
"We are looking for a fall because OPEC has really failed to deliver," said one broker. "I'm rather surprised it rallied the way it did. I think there was some panic buying yesterday."
OPEC leaders on Thursday confirmed the previous day's deal to stick to previously agreed production ceilings and wrapped up proceedings with renewed vows of quota dispcipline.
The market barely slowed its downward slide on the news.
Market doubt swung on statements by Venezuelan oil minister Erwin Arrieta that his country was not over-producing.

His remarks raised eyebrows as his country is assessed to be pumping out 800,000 bpd over its quota. Brokers said Caracas and other quota-busters appeared to be immediately slipping back into the habit of just paying lip service to output limits.

"Few, if any, of the oil ministers concerned have made supportive comments so far and clearly it will be impossible to police any continuing overproduction," GNI Ltd said in its daily research report.
